tob-13149: Four hundred twenty-three verses of the Buddha’s teaching, gathered into twenty-six chapters on themes like the mind, the self, and the path. The Dhammapada is Buddhism’s most quoted scripture — concise, practical, and aimed at daily life rather than doctrine. This English version preserves the directness that has made it beloved across two thousand years.
tob-4049: The first volume of Wordsworth’s gathered poems holds the work of his firebrand youth — the Lyrical Ballads years, when he and Coleridge remade English verse in plain speech. Here are the daffodils, the leech-gatherer, and the first great nature lyrics. The volume opens the lifework of England’s poet of the plain human heart.
tob-4249: Steiner’s Outline of Occult Science lays out his whole world-scheme — the ripening of world and man through Saturn, Sun, Moon, and Earth turns, and the road of awakening. Close-packed but orderly, it is Anthroposophy’s chief textbook. Here is Steiner the system-builder at full stretch.
tob-13749: Madame Guyon, the French holy woman jailed for her teaching, penned this brief guide to heart-prayer — turning inward, resting in God’s nearness, letting words and ways fall off. Her ‘short method’ spread still worship across Europe. The booklet stays the classic of inward prayer.
tob-4149: Edward Henry Palmer’s Sacred Books Qur’an — this first volume — gives the fore-half of Islam’s writ in clear Victorian English. His scholar’s rendering served readers for generations. The volume made the Qur’an open to the English-speaking world. Palmer’s toil stays honored for its faithfulness.
arxiv-2605-08749: Machine-learning models compress information into hidden codes called latents, and this 2026 paper by Mikhail Parakhin, André M. Carvalho, and Patrick Haluptzok proposes a new training objective for them: the wristband Gaussian loss. It decomposes latents into a sphere component and an interval component, aiming for codes that behave deterministically and combine cleanly. The target is more reliable, composable representations for generative models.
arxiv-2605-08849: In swirling flows — think of water draining or air in a turbine — the swirl sometimes flips direction without warning. Eman Bagheri, Riccardo Casali, and Stefan Becker disentangle the coherent structures behind this swirl-switching, tracing where the flip originates. The 2026 paper is fluid-dynamics research on a phenomenon engineers would love to predict.
arxiv-2605-08949: Teaching a language model new tricks usually erases old ones — catastrophic forgetting. Binghang Lu, Zheyuan Deng, Runyu Zhang, and colleagues fight it with Muon-OGD, projecting gradients onto spectral-orthogonal directions under the Muon optimizer so new learning does not trample the old. The 2026 paper targets continual learning that actually continues.
arxiv-2605-09449: Video models that understand space egocentrically — from the camera's view — get lost when the viewpoint changes. Bo Gu, Zhikang Zhang, Zizhuang Wei, and colleagues build allocentric cognitive maps instead: SpaceMind++, for spatially grounded video models. The 2026 paper gives AI a map, not just a view.
arxiv-2605-09649: Long contexts balloon the KV cache until memory bursts; evicting the right tokens at the right time saves the day. Ngoc Bui, Hieu Trung Nguyen, Arman Cohan, and Rex Ying make each token count with intelligent eviction policies. The 2026 paper is long-context efficiency for memory-starved deployments.
arxiv-2605-09749: Discrete diffusion models generate tokens step by step, but constraints — grammar, validity, safety — must be enforced during decoding itself. Federico Tomasi, Dmitrii Moor, Alice Wang, and Mounia Lalmas guide decoding with primal-dual methods. The 2026 paper keeps generated text legal.
arxiv-2605-09849: Outcomes can be hidden — unmeasured, latent — but proximal causal inference handles them anyway. Helen Guo, Ilya Shpitser, and Elizabeth L. Ogburn develop proximal causal inference for hidden outcomes. The 2026 paper is causal inference for outcomes you cannot directly observe today.
arxiv-2605-09949: SMILES strings encode molecules as text; translation models learn to map them — and chirality, the handedness of molecules, emerges from syntax to semantics. Zehao Li, Yasuhiro Yoshikai, Shumpei Nemoto, and colleagues unveil the emergence. The 2026 paper is chemical AI discovering handedness. It finds handedness where only syntax was expected.
arxiv-2605-10049: Transient execution attacks — Spectre-class exploits — need compiler-based defenses built on ARM hardware primitives: Janus. Ciyan Ouyang, Peinan Li, Yubiao Huang, and colleagues build the defense. The 2026 paper is hardware security compiled in. It defends silicon at compile time.
arxiv-2605-10149: Temporal action segmentation — labeling actions in video over time — improved via constraint-aware decoding. Yeo Keat Ee, Debaditya Roy, Chen Li, and colleagues develop the decoder. The 2026 paper is video understanding with rules. It segments actions while respecting hard constraints.
pmc-13426349: SLCO1B1 gene polymorphisms in high-altitude residents with type 2 diabetes — dyslipidemic versus normolipidemic patients compared. pmc-13475349: Adolescent fertility from 1950 to 2023 — levels and trends among 10-to-19-year-olds across 201 countries and areas. pmc-13474249: Encapsulated L-lysine — from physicochemical properties to broiler responses. Hosna Hajati, Amirhossein Alizadeh Ghamsari, and colleagues feed the chickens. pmc-13472149: An antibiotic-degrading synthetic ecosystem — population dynamics and cross-feeding, revealed by single-cell Raman spectroscopy and stable isotope probing. Rui Xue, Xuan Wu, Rong Ji, and colleagues probe the community. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is synthetic ecology. It watches microbes share the antibiotic-degrading work.
pmc-13454349: The microbiome in cancer — a systems-level regulator of immune, metabolic, neural, and endocrine signaling. Jhommara Bautista and Andrés López-Cortés write the synthesis. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cancer microbiome. It casts gut bugs as master regulators.
pmc-13454049: Glioblastoma as a neuro-immune network disorder — rethinking the tumor microenvironment, neural circuit integration, and therapeutic resistance. Tyler Lo, Armando Bunjaj, Jeffrey P. Turnbull, and colleagues reframe the tumor. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is glioblastoma biology. It rewires how we see brain cancer.
pmc-13426449: Acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery — in low- and middle-income countries. Emmanuel Ndaba and Vukosi Baloyi review the burden. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cardiac AKI. It counts kidney injury where resources are thin. Kidneys, at risk. Surgery, cardiac.
pmc-13408049: An irreparable massive rotator cuff tear — arthroscopic rotator cable reconstruction with dermal allograft tuberoplasty augmentation. Alexander R Markes and James P Bradley do the reconstruction. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is shoulder surgery. It cables a shoulder beyond repair. Rotator cuff, reconstructed.
arxiv-2606-17249: Emre Can Kızılateş squeezes FastGRNN, a compact recurrent network, onto ultra-constrained microcontrollers. From compression to deployment, the paper shows real-time, energy-efficient inference on chips with kilobytes of memory. The work brings machine learning to sensors and wearables that cannot afford the cloud.
arxiv-2606-17349: C. A. S. Almeida shows that operator ordering ambiguities in twisted bilayer graphene act as an emergent gauge field. In the magic-angle material, the order of quantum operations leaves singular spectral signatures, fingerprints in the energy spectrum. The result deepens the theory of graphene's most mysterious phase.
arxiv-2606-17649: Yuxiang Luo, Chen Wang, and Nan Tang decompose the risk of fine-tuning before it happens. Their pre-hoc framework predicts how a model will perform after tuning, without running the expensive process. Teams can screen ideas cheaply and invest training budgets where they pay off.
arxiv-2606-17849: Roman Wußler and colleagues create squeezed and non-classical collective motional many-body states through stroboscopic Rydberg dressing. The pulsed interaction sculpts atomic motion into quantum-correlated dances. These states promise sensors beyond classical limits. The stroboscopic technique works with existing Rydberg atom array hardware.
arxiv-2606-17949: Wei Da and Evangelia Kalyvianaki present RouteBalance, fusing model routing and load balancing for heterogeneous LLM serving. Different models on different hardware need smart traffic control. The fused approach routes each request to the best model-server pair. The result is cheaper, faster inference at scale.
arxiv-2606-18049: Jan Voets and colleagues reformulate counterfactual generation for time series forecasting with ConTex. Asking what would have happened requires careful counterfactuals in temporal data. Their reformulation makes the explanations faithful to the dynamics. Better counterfactuals mean better decisions from forecasts.
arxiv-2606-18149: Soheil Radfar systematically benchmarks inverse physics-informed neural networks, asking how sparse and how noisy the data can be. The study maps the breaking points of PINNs on inverse problems. Knowing the limits guides practitioners toward solvable formulations. It is a reality check for physics-informed AI.
arxiv-2606-18249: Wujian Peng and colleagues unify multimodal autoregressive modeling with shared context, arguing the visual tokenizer is key. One tokenizer for images and text lets a single model think across modalities. The unified approach simplifies the messy landscape of multimodal AI. Their experiments show the shared context paying off on vision-language tasks.
plos-pone-0003449: Mycologists mapped the key diagnostic flag of a fungal disease in this 2008 paper. Histoplasmosis, caused by the fungus Histoplasma capsulatum, is diagnosed through antibodies against its M antigen, yet the protein's function was unknown. The team charted the antigen's biology and molecular map in the fungus's yeast phase, strengthening both diagnosis and understanding of the pathogen.
plos-pone-0003549: Malaria researchers weakened the parasite at a key checkpoint in this 2008 study. Deleting the p52 gene of Plasmodium falciparum stalled the parasite's development in the liver stage, the quiet phase before it invades the blood. The attenuated parasite is a candidate for whole-parasite vaccines, which have shown more promise than subunit shots.
plos-pone-0003649: In 2008, Rajagovindan and Ding took apart a brain rhythm puzzle. Brain areas often fire in sync with almost no delay, a near-zero phase lag that is hard to explain, and the team broke that synchrony into parts. Their take shows how brain networks can line up their beats so tightly, a trick thought to link what we sense with what we recall.
plos-pone-0003749: In 2008, Perron, Quessy, and Bell found healthy carriers hiding drug-proof germs. Drug-resistant pathogenic bacteria turned up in hosts with no symptoms, a silent reservoir. The finding means resistance can spread quietly, complicating efforts to track and contain it.
plos-pone-0003849: Working in 2008, a team surveyed stomach-bug strains in cancer patients. Helicobacter pylori genotypes, especially the vacA and cagA variants, were compared between patients with and without gastric cancer. The high diversity found complicates the hunt for which strain features actually drive tumors.
plos-pone-0003949: In 2008, Jeong, Wang, and Guimaraes found a cancer gene that starts but cannot finish the job. BRAF activation kicked off invasive prostate tumors in mice yet could not maintain them. The split role suggests BRAF matters for initiation more than progression.
plos-pone-0004049: In 2009, Brookfield, Cheung, and Yang asked if cancer care should centralize. They studied whether high-volume hospitals improve outcomes in gynecologic cancer. Patient chances for cure and palliation were compared across different hospital types. The results inform the heated regionalization debate in women's cancer care.
plos-pone-0004149: In 2009, Homsy, Bunnell, and Moore followed women on HIV treatment in Uganda. The prospective study tracked pregnancy plans and outcomes on antiretroviral therapy. ART's effect on childbearing wishes became clearer over time. The findings guide family planning for women with HIV.
plos-pone-0004249: In 2009, Tu, Yang, and Tsai found two genes building fish hearts. Nkx2.7 and Nkx2.5 worked redundantly in zebrafish heart formation. Losing both stalled cardiac morphogenesis fully. The pair's teamwork illuminates congenital heart defects. The fish genes mirror the human tinman family.
plos-pone-0004349: In 2009, Pang, Singh, and Gao designed much safer bug killers. Selective irreversible inhibitors of aphid acetylcholinesterases were carefully crafted. The compounds spared human enzymes entirely. The steps advance human-safe insecticides greatly. The work targets pests that ravage world crops yearly.
plos-pone-0004449: In 2009, Alghisi, Ponsonnet, and Rüegg found a cancer drug flipping its target. The integrin blocker cilengitide switched its target on instead of off. The switch broke vessel-wall junctions. The finding reshapes vessel-drug design. The paradox demands fresh thinking today.
plos-pone-0004549: In 2009, Lehmann, Hume, and Licht traced an arms race in deadly malaria mosquitoes. Molecular evolution of immune genes in Anopheles gambiae was mapped. The mosquito alleles fought back parasites. The finding maps host-parasite coevolution today. The natural selection was strong indeed.
plos-pone-0004649: In 2009, Williams, Lim, and Harr linked a wobbly gene copy to mouse anxiety. A common unstable copy number variant tracked Glo1 expression and anxiety. The extra copies raised anxiety-like behavior measurably. The finding maps anxiety genetics. The variant is common.
plos-pone-0004749: In 2009, Wallen, Thompson, and Reilly found a chemo drug extending killer T-cell life. Fludarabine modulated immune response and extended CD8 T cell survival in vivo. The transferred cells lived longer indeed. The finding aids immunotherapy research. The therapy is adoptive.
plos-pone-0358849: Knowing your child breathes polluted air on the way to school is distressing — and this paper named the trap: the awareness-distress paradox. Surveying parents of urban schoolchildren in a northeastern province, it showed that greater awareness of traffic pollution tracks with greater psychological distress. The paradox asks whether information alone harms without action.
plos-pone-0358749: Expansive soils swell when wet and crack when dry, wrecking roads and foundations. This experimental study tested LSP-stabilized expansive soil under repeated drying-wetting cycles. The engineering performance data show whether the stabilization holds through the seasons.
plos-pone-0358549: Subway accidents cascade — one failure triggers the next. This paper combined complex network analysis with accident data to comprehensively identify key risk factors in subway operations. The network map shows operators which failures to prevent first.
plos-pone-0358449: Loneliness may be rooted in ancient emotional systems wired long before language. This paper studied relationships between primal emotional systems and the sense of loneliness, with early maladaptive schemas as the mediator. The model traces how deep emotional wiring hardens into adult isolation — and where therapy might intervene.
plos-pone-0358049: Deepfakes leave spectral fingerprints invisible to the human eye. This paper used dual-domain self-supervised feature alignment via spectral–spatial representation learning for deepfake anomaly detection. The method spots manipulated media by the traces that pixels alone can’t hide.
plos-pone-0344649: Red drum fish sing in choruses to spawn — and boat noise drowns out the music. This study measured the impacts of vessel noise on red drum spawning choruses in Saint Andrew Bay, Florida. The findings show that noisy waters mean fewer fish babies, with direct consequences for the fishery.
plos-pone-0356549: Asian elephants can restrain their own impulses — a hallmark of advanced intelligence. This study demonstrated that they exhibit inhibitory control in a detour task, resisting the direct route to reach a reward. The elephants’ self-control places them among cognition’s elite alongside apes and corvids.
plos-pone-0356249: A troodontid dinosaur from Montana’s Two Medicine Formation gets the full anatomical treatment. This paper described the pelvic and hindlimb osteology and ontogeny of the Cretaceous predator — how its bones looked and how they changed as it grew. The growth series reveals how these intelligent, bird-like dinosaurs developed from hatchling to hunter.
plos-pone-0357049: Pregnant women with hypertensive disorders in low- and middle-income countries navigate dangerous care gaps. This scoping review protocol will systematically map their health-seeking behaviors. The planned review aims to inform interventions that meet these mothers where they actually are.
plos-pone-0355549: Designing new peptide drugs for G protein-coupled receptors — the targets of a third of all medicines — is getting an AI upgrade. This paper assessed generative de novo peptide design methods for GPCRs. The evaluation shows which AI approaches actually produce viable drug candidates.
plos-pone-0354749: Plants surviving on cangas — Amazonian ironstone outcrops — are botanical marvels. This case study examined the structural adaptations of aboveground vegetative organs in Carajasia cangae, a Rubiaceae species from these harsh habitats. The adaptations reveal how life thrives on nearly pure iron rock.
plos-pone-0355749: Chinese immigrant caregivers of autistic children need education built with them, not for them. This paper described creating a caregiver education program through a community-engaged process with Chinese caregivers. The co-designed program respects cultural values while delivering the practical skills families need.
plos-pone-0347949: Speech-language pathologists in Canada serve increasingly diverse clients — cultural safety is essential. This paper published a scoping review protocol tracing the path from cultural awareness to safety in Canadian speech-language pathology practice. The planned review will map how the profession is — or isn’t — rising to the challenge.
plos-pone-0355649: Data envelopment analysis — measuring efficiency — gets sharper when self-efficiency is decomposed. This paper did so with a cross-efficiency-based quantity–price framework. The methodological advance gives economists and managers a finer instrument for judging who’s truly efficient and why.
plos-pone-0343349: Mobile money is transforming fragile states — especially for women and youth. This paper examined its welfare effects in Mozambique. The findings show digital finance reaching where banks never did — with measurable improvements in the lives of those conflict and poverty hit hardest.
plos-pone-0353849: Predicting life expectancy accurately — and interpretably — matters for policy and pensions. This paper built a multi-stage stacking framework for accurate, interpretable life expectancy modeling. The stacked models balance predictive power with the transparency that public decisions demand.
plos-pone-0352249: Abu Dhabi’s urban seas — mangroves and seagrass beds — may shelter surprising marine life. This first eDNA-based monitoring of marine vertebrates in the emirate’s urban ecosystem tested that hypothesis. The environmental DNA reveals biodiversity reservoirs hiding beside one of the world’s busiest coastlines.
plos-pone-0354249: Zebrafish — biology’s favorite vertebrate — need automated body measurement at scale. This paper developed automatic morphometric analysis of adult zebrafish using microCT. The 3D measurement pipeline accelerates the phenotyping underpinning genetic and toxicology research.
plos-pone-0339949: Clean cookstoves — the Poriborton trial in Bangladesh — had spillover effects on who cares for babies and does housework. This paper measured those effects on infant caregiving and domestic work. The findings reveal how a stove intervention reshapes household labor — with implications for women’s time and children’s care.
plos-pone-0354149: Rectal dosimetry during prostate radiotherapy — with an in vivo dosimeter carrying an MRI marker. This paper developed it. The device measures the radiation dose the rectum actually receives — visible on MRI. The findings promise safer prostate cancer treatment — sparing the bowel while targeting the tumor.
plos-pone-0351249: Postoperative foot pain — worsened by TNF-alpha via Nav1.8 sodium channel regulation. This paper demonstrated the mechanism. The findings linked inflammation to pain’s molecular machinery. The research nominates targets for the pain that lingers after the incision heals — precision analgesia.
plos-pone-0353949: HIV disclosure decision aids — selecting one for Georgian adaptation via nominal group technique. This paper did so. The structured consensus chose the tool worth translating. The findings respected local expertise — the best aid selected by those who’ll use it.
plos-pone-0353349: RF-aided NOMA visible light networks — resource optimization via joint blocklength control and power allocation. This paper built that algorithm. The optimization balanced the light-based network’s competing demands. The findings advanced LiFi — internet through illumination, efficiently managed.
plos-pone-0351649: Jeddah’s dengue virus isolate — epidemiologically and genomically analyzed. This paper did so with therapeutic implications. The Saudi strain’s genome revealed its evolutionary story. The findings informed future drug development — knowing the enemy’s exact genetic face.
plos-pone-0352149: Honey bees facing thermal stress — protected by probiotics and prebiotics buffering survival and antioxidant enzymes. This paper demonstrated it. The microbial supplements fortified bees against heat. The findings offered a tool for pollinator protection — as climate change turns up the hive’s temperature.
plos-pone-0352649: HIV-1 Nef — inhibiting JAK/STAT signaling by inducing proteasomal degradation of STAT1. This paper demonstrated the mechanism. The findings revealed how the virus dismantles interferon defenses. The research exposed the viral sabotage — Nef as the immune system’s quiet assassin.
plos-pone-0352349: High-impact science — network hedging’s role in negotiating knowledge production. This paper studied it. The analysis showed how scientists hedge their collaborations. Its sociology value is the strategy. The work maps the safety nets behind breakthroughs. The hedging concept is the insight: scientists diversify collaborators the way investors diversify portfolios, managing career risk.
plos-pone-0351849: Glioblastoma lactylation genes — immunological characteristics revealed by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing. This paper did so. plos-pone-0346949: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic patients — air pollution mixtures’ individual and combined effects on cardiovascular risk. This paper studied them. The analysis untangled the toxic cocktail. Its environmental cardiology value is the mixture. The work parses the air’s assault on the vulnerable heart.
plos-pone-0352449: California Marine Protected Areas — conservation impacts demonstrated with large-scale participatory science data. This paper did so. The analysis turned divers’ observations into evidence. Its marine value is the proof. The work shows the protected areas working, through citizens’ eyes.
plos-pone-0350749: The Hungarian Skindex-Mini — reliability and construct validity. This paper tested them. The analysis validated the brief skin questionnaire. The finding adapts the dermatology tool. The work gives Hungary its mini skin index. The Mini format is the practicality: three questions that capture what longer dermatology scales measure.
plos-pone-0319549: US allopathic medical schools — gender discrimination and personal-professional development. This paper studied the fostering. The analysis asked whether the schools nurture equitably. The finding is the gap. The work grades the medical school’s gender climate. The allopathic focus is the scope: it examines the MD-granting schools specifically, not osteopathic or international ones.
plos-pone-0351949: Diesel-methanol engine ignition timing — optimal function from combustion duration, load, and blending ratio. This paper determined it. The analysis tuned the dual-fuel burn. The finding times the spark. The work fires the methanol-diesel at the perfect moment. The blending ratio is the variable: it tunes the timing as the methanol fraction changes.
europmc-pmc2828549: Antidepressants of the SSRI type may work partly by dulling emotional extremes. This 2010 brain-imaging study finds diminished neural processing of both aversive and rewarding stimuli during SSRI treatment. The authors show the drugs tone down responses to good and bad alike. The result helps explain the emotional blunting some patients report.
europmc-pmc2829049: Stickleback fish kept evolving the same traits in apart lakes, a gift to science. This 2010 paper uses DNA tag reads to probe their gene pools. The team finds the gene roots of replayed change. The study became a star case of watching nature rerun its tricks.
europmc-pmc2837749: During the 2009 H1N1 pandemic, severe obesity emerged as a danger factor. This 2010 paper quantifies morbid obesity as a risk factor for hospitalization and death from pandemic influenza. The authors analyze surveillance data to measure the risk. The finding changed triage and vaccination priorities for future flu pandemics.
europmc-pmc2936549: After a bout of salmonella gut trouble, resident germs help finish the cleanup. This 2010 paper shows the gut's own microbes clear leftover germs after mild Salmonella. The authors reveal teamwork in recovery. Their work highlights the flora's guard role. The gut's own tenants prove to be allies.
europmc-pmc2946949: Flipped chromosome chunks steer evolution, and this 2010 paper tells how and why they spread. The author pulls together theory on how flips are born, grow, and fade. Their frame clears up a classic riddle. The paper became a key reference. Students still learn flip genetics from it.
europmc-pmc3017849: Grape aroma genes got mapped. This 2010 paper lists the grapevine genes that brew floral and piney scents. The authors reveal the scent makers. Their work aids wine science. Muscats owe their perfume to these genes. Breeders now select for bouquet by DNA.
europmc-pmc3041749: Gene assembly got modular. This 2011 paper presents a modular cloning system for standardized assembly of multigene constructs. The authors' Golden Gate system spread through synthetic biology. Their method sped plant engineering. Parts snap together like molecular Lego. Crop engineers build traits in weeks.
europmc-pmc3043049: Smokers' lungs host altered germs. This 2011 paper compares lung germs in healthy smokers and COPD patients. The authors reveal the microbial shift. Their work links smoke to lung disease. COPD lungs teem with troublemakers. Quitting may restore the healthy mix.
europmc-pmc3046449: Breast lumps got a new ultrasound test. This 2010 paper tests stiffness-mapping ultrasound on solid breast lumps. The authors' maps aid diagnosis. Their work spread through radiology. Hard lumps raise more suspicion than soft ones. Biopsy rates dropped where the test spread.
europmc-pmc3072949: Ovarian cancer cells swallow tiny bubbles. This 2011 paper shows ovarian tumor cells gulp bubble-packets from their surroundings. The authors reveal the swallowing. Their work points to delivery tricks. Drug-loaded bubbles could ride the same route. The bubbles may also spread the cancer.
europmc-pmc3112149: Short chromosome caps signal cancer risk. This 2011 meta-analysis links shortened telomeres to higher cancer risk. The authors pool the evidence. Their work points to screening. europmc-pmc3175149: An alarm cytokine got reviewed. This 2011 paper covers IL-33's role in inflammation and disease. The author maps the cytokine's reach. Their overview guides drug design. europmc-pmc3228849: Malaria relapses got their timing explained. This 2011 paper reviews what sets relapse timing in vivax malaria. The author maps the triggers. Their work guides treatment. europmc-pmc3310649: A new tick germ infected Russians. This 2011 paper reports the first Borrelia miyamotoi cases in Russia. The authors reveal the cases. Their work guides doctors. The germ mimicked Lyme disease. Platonov's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3320549: Gene-silencing enzymes got a review. This 2012 paper reviews histone deacetylases in gene regulation. The authors map the paradigms. Their overview guides drug research. europmc-pmc3323649: Gut acids fought obesity. This 2012 paper shows two gut acids fight diet-induced obesity in mice. The authors reveal the hormones. Their work guides nutrition. Appetite hormones shifted, they found. Lin's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3342149: Fibroids got a women's survey. This 2012 survey asked 21,746 women about fibroid symptoms. The authors reveal the burden. Their work guides care. Heavy bleeding topped the complaints. Zimmermann's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped fibroid care.
europmc-pmc3349649: Heart immune cells got discovered. This 2012 paper finds a distinct immune-cell population in the adult mouse heart. The authors reveal the profile. Their work guides cardiology. Pinto's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It launched a subfield.
europmc-pmc3389649: Immune peacekeepers got an adenosine brake. This 2012 paper shows the adenosine-A2A pathway steers regulatory T cells. The authors reveal the brake. Their work guides immunotherapy. Ohta's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped cancer therapy.
europmc-pmc3396849: Calcium got an energy dial. This 2012 paper reviews how mitochondrial calcium steers ATP production. The authors map the control. Their overview guides cell biology. Tarasov's review is widely cited. It is a classic. It shaped metabolism research. The review is widely taught.
europmc-pmc3399849: Lung scarring got a cleanup review. This 2012 paper reviews autophagy, cell cleanup, in lung fibrosis. The authors map the role. Their overview guides therapy. Patel's review is widely cited. It is a classic. It shaped IPF research. The review is widely taught.
europmc-pmc3424049: Reactive oxygen got a health review. This 2012 paper reviews reactive oxygen's roles in health and disease. The authors map the roles. Their overview guides medicine. europmc-pmc6556049: Drug designers dock candidate molecules into protein targets on computers - but judging how close two poses are gets tricky when the molecule is symmetric. europmc-pmc6601349: HIV's toll in sub-Saharan Africa varies block by block - national averages hide the hotspots. The high-resolution picture lets health workers aim testing and treatment at the neighborhoods that need them most.
europmc-pmc6683149: With age, muscles wither - and gut microbes may be accomplices. This review links the aging microbiome to shrinking muscle mass and strength, spotlighting frailty and sarcopenia. The gut-muscle axis suggests probiotics or diet tweaks could one day keep older bodies stronger.
europmc-pmc6784249: Night owls forced into early schedules live with 'social jetlag' - a chronic mismatch between body clock and social clock. The chronotype pioneer behind the Munich questionnaire offers a self-critical review of 15 years of research. The takeaway: when you sleep is biology, not character.
europmc-pmc6814749: Losing sight in old age often starts with macular degeneration - but which retinal cells go wrong? This single-cell atlas of the human retina pinpoints the cell types tied to age-related macular degeneration genes. The cellular map turns genetic clues into real suspects. Knowing the culprits focuses the hunt for cures.
